progressionAssessment.rationale: All exact workbook terms and formal prerequisites pass. Literary introduction and stylistics precede advanced literary research; rhetoric precedes its practice module; film introduction precedes documentary and adaptation; introductory sociology precedes Modern Sociology; modern history precedes the source-based seminar. Level-three Philosophy of Emotion has no formal prerequisite and is placed in the final semester.

basisLabels: Literary interpretation, genres, stylistics and creative expression
courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Literary Studies directly teaches practical criticism, fiction, poetry, drama and narrative form, supplying the literary-analysis foundation. It implements the explicit academic basis “Literary interpretation, genres, stylistics and creative expression”.

basisLabels: Rhetorical communication and public speaking
courseTraceability.rationale: The Art of Rhetorical Communication directly teaches argument, rhetorical theory and persuasive writing/speaking, contributing to the target communication strand without implying English-proficiency instruction. It implements the explicit academic basis “Rhetorical communication and public speaking”.

basisLabels: High and popular culture, historical society and English-speaking cultural worlds
courseTraceability.rationale: Modern History provides specific complementary modern historical study of industrialisation, sovereignty, war, welfare and decolonisation needed to interpret nineteenth-/twentieth-century cultural works; it is not British history alone. It implements the explicit academic basis “High and popular culture, historical society and English-speaking cultural worlds”.

basisLabels: Literary interpretation, genres, stylistics and creative expression
courseTraceability.rationale: Great Literary Works directly studies literary genres, primary texts and their historical themes across Western literary heritage; it is not a dedicated survey of British or American periods. It implements the explicit academic basis “Literary interpretation, genres, stylistics and creative expression”.

alternativeSelection.assessment: One complete related-fields response is defensible. The literature/culture specialization is substantively covered by that curriculum and does not establish a second distinct direction. The first proposed additional direction, English structural/historical/global linguistics, lacks a cumulative language-specific sequence: stylistics and Psycholinguistics provide limited contributions, not phonology, syntax, historical linguistics or world-English sociolinguistics. Advanced proficiency also lacks a dedicated development sequence. English being used in science, politics and business does not evidence a coherent independent curriculum in those three fields. Teaching was assessed through Rhetoric in Action, Psycholinguistics, brain/behaviour foundations and lifespan development: these do not establish a complete English-learning/secondary pedagogy curriculum. Its rejection concerns academic content, not professional qualification alone. Stop at one; no third alternative is attempted.

notes.text: Radboud combines English proficiency, linguistics and sustained British/American literary study with independent research. This UCR programme approaches literary and cultural questions through literature, rhetoric, media and history. It provides related fields rather than the full English Language and Culture curriculum: dedicated English proficiency, phonetics, phonology, syntax and historical-English study are absent, and its British literary-period coverage is less extensive.

audience.programmeDescription: Explore English language, literature and culture through language development, linguistics, British and other English-speaking literary traditions, and independent research. The English Language and Culture track is distinct from American Studies.
audience.comparisonExplanation: This UCR programme offers a sustained route through literary interpretation, stylistics, creative expression, film and cultural history. Its literature and cultural-analysis content responds to an important part of English Studies. It does not reproduce dedicated English proficiency, phonetics, phonology, syntax or historical-English training, or the full British literary-period sequence.
